title: School SLP credential and operator-fit comparison
scope: Six-state comparison for an independently operated staffing agency placing qualified SLPs in public schools. This is a requirements-research map, not a comprehensive legal determination or permission to start practice.
method: Official professional-board, education-agency, legislative and compact-commission sources. The employment relationship and service setting matter; direct-school employee exemptions are not automatically available to agency personnel.
comparative_inference: Texas and North Carolina have comparatively clear professional-license school pathways. Virginia expressly addresses contractor-paid school SLPs. Maryland has a defined license route plus a material contracting-agency employment-history review. New York has an explicit dual-credential requirement for the agency model. Georgia needs the selected district to resolve the school-certificate and professional-license combination. These observations are not a ranking of market demand, therapist supply, cost, or procurement access.
principles: Initial pilot design: qualified, experienced, fully licensed SLPs. Do not depend on assistants, aides, clinical fellows, emergency credentials, provisional supervision or exemptions to make the first economics work.
OT and PT are separate professions with separate boards, scopes, supervision rules and compact statuses. Do not reuse the SLP credential decision as their authorization.
Keep professional authority, school-role credentials, school clearance, contract approval and payer eligibility as separate requirements with individual evidence and expiration fields.
An ASHA certificate is evidence relevant to some applications; it is not automatically a state practice license or a school clearance.
Compact membership is not an issued privilege. Verify a clinician's actual authority in the state of service before assignment; no compact benefit is assumed for these six pilot candidates.

The proposed AI system may collect documents, check completeness, flag expiration and prepare a credential packet. Accountable people resolve applicability, exceptions and final assignment eligibility.

No provider records were queried, applicants registered, districts contacted or applications submitted during this research. No turnaround, cost or available-worker advantage is claimed from the existence of a licensing pathway.

compact_snapshot.observation: The Commission page reviewed on October 20, 2026 lists registration open for practitioners in Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee and West Virginia. It says other member states must complete onboarding and compact requirements before issuing privileges.
compact_snapshot.member_evidence: The Commission's member-state delegate list includes Georgia, North Carolina, Virginia and Maryland. Texas and New York are not established as operational routes by the reviewed evidence.
compact_snapshot.planning_rule: Use active individual state licensure for pilot feasibility. Recheck the Commission and the relevant board if considering an actual compact privilege; a map, bill, membership or home-state license is not proof that the individual may start.

state_profiles.name: Texas
state_profiles.credential_path: TEA's assignment rule permits professionally licensed SLPs to provide school speech services within their license scope. It also lists particular school speech credentials; the pilot should use the current TDLR professional-license route rather than rely on a school-only legacy route.
state_profiles.school_specific_requirement: Continuing contractor services with direct, unsupervised student contact trigger school fingerprint requirements. TEA describes different handling for qualified school contractors and other contractors, including district access through LEE FAST/FACT.
state_profiles.compact_relevance: See shared compact snapshot; no operational compact route established by this review.
state_profiles.practice_licensing_notes: TDLR publishes the professional SLP application requirements, including graduate education, experience, examinations and criminal-history review. Do not interpret an application or an out-of-state license as a Texas credential.
new_operator_questions: Will the district classify the agency as a qualified school contractor, and who initiates and receives each required background result?
Which district certifications, registries, orientation and credential packet are required before student contact?
Does the actual contract require an ASHA credential, prior school experience, bilingual qualification or other conditions beyond state licensure?
state_profiles.evidence_limit: Professional-license acceptance and school screening structure are documented. District vendor approval, procurement eligibility, business registration, insurance and clinical availability remain unverified.

state_profiles.name: North Carolina
state_profiles.credential_path: NC DPI states that, effective July 1, 2011, a current valid NCBOESLPA license is the qualifying school SLP credential. The board offers a reciprocal application pathway for holders of an active, full, unrestricted license in another state.
state_profiles.school_specific_requirement: DPI describes a subsequent licensure-section submission using the board license and education/experience documents. Confirm with the district which DPI/pay-authorization steps apply to contracted agency staff rather than direct district employees.
state_profiles.compact_relevance: Member status documented. See shared compact snapshot; no operational benefit assumed.
state_profiles.practice_licensing_notes: The reciprocal pathway is an application for a North Carolina license. The board says practice must wait for issuance unless a statutory exemption actually applies; this pilot does not rely on such an exemption.
new_operator_questions: Which district background checks, health clearances, training and system access are required for agency therapists?
Is DPI pay authorization relevant to this particular agency arrangement, or only to district payroll?
Are additional payer enrollment or service documentation requirements part of the district contract?
state_profiles.evidence_limit: The school qualifying credential is explicit. The reviewed sources do not establish one universal agency onboarding packet or a guaranteed reciprocal-application processing time.

state_profiles.name: Georgia
state_profiles.credential_path: Two distinct pathways appear in primary materials: the professional board's SLP license and GaPSC's P–12 Speech and Language Pathology service certificate. GaPSC accepts a qualifying preparation program, ASHA certification or a Georgia professional license as a basis, plus the applicable special requirements.
state_profiles.school_specific_requirement: GaPSC's published rule identifies the school service certificate and its Praxis/standards requirements. The exact combination required for a private staffing-agency placement, including any lawful school-only exemption, remains a district-and-board applicability question; do not presume either credential automatically substitutes for the other.
state_profiles.compact_relevance: Member status documented. See shared compact snapshot; no operational benefit assumed.
state_profiles.practice_licensing_notes: The board's licensure-by-certification checklist includes ASHA verification, other-state license verification and a national background check. A professional-license background check does not by itself prove school contractor clearance.
new_operator_questions: Must this contract's agency SLPs hold both the board license and GaPSC service certificate, and is a separate clearance certificate relevant?
Who sponsors and verifies school certification and the district's criminal-history screening?
Do district charter or waiver provisions affect personnel requirements for this specific assignment?
state_profiles.evidence_limit: Both credential systems are verified, but this review does not settle the agency-specific exemption or district variation. Do not score Georgia as simpler than other states from the existence of multiple routes.

state_profiles.name: Virginia
state_profiles.credential_path: Virginia's professional board guidance expressly permits an SLP placed and paid by a private contractor in a public school division to hold a school, provisional or full BASLP license. The proposed pilot uses fully licensed SLPs; school-only and provisional routes remain separately scoped alternatives.
state_profiles.school_specific_requirement: School-only licensure is a professional-board credential with setting/funding restrictions. Applicable school contracts involving direct student contact must require contractor certification concerning specified criminal convictions.
state_profiles.compact_relevance: Member status documented. See shared compact snapshot; no operational benefit assumed.
state_profiles.practice_licensing_notes: The contractor pathway is expressly addressed, which improves requirements clarity. It does not remove district qualifications or the supervision obligations of a provisional route.
new_operator_questions: What additional fingerprinting, abuse-registry checks, training and onboarding evidence does the district contract require?
Does the agency arrangement and funding fit the setting restrictions if school-only licenses are ever considered?
Which personnel and business approvals must be complete before the district issues an assignment or purchase order?
state_profiles.evidence_limit: The public-school contractor license interpretation is documented. This is not proof of open purchasing access, therapist supply, rapid licensing or agency-wide clearance.

state_profiles.name: Maryland
state_profiles.credential_path: Maryland requires the professional board license for school SLP hires from October 1, 2007 onward. The narrow continuously employed pre-2007 exemption is not a suitable assumption for a new staffing operator.
state_profiles.school_specific_requirement: A contracting agency must carry out the statutory employment-history review for personnel with direct contact with minors, maintain the required records, disclose required information to schools and honor school objections to assignment. This is a separate workflow from a criminal check.
state_profiles.compact_relevance: Member status documented. See shared compact snapshot; no operational benefit assumed.
state_profiles.practice_licensing_notes: The statute permits a limited pending-application route only after board preliminary approval and a completed application. Do not equate application submission with approval. A universal extra educator credential for ordinary contracted SLPs was not established in this review.
new_operator_questions: How will the agency perform, document and disclose the required employment-history review?
Which fingerprinting, child-protection checks and additional district credentials apply?
Does the selected role or service model require any additional agency approval, professional entity structure or payer enrollment?
state_profiles.evidence_limit: Professional licensing and contracting-agency history-review obligations are documented. District-specific onboarding and additional entity requirements are not settled.

state_profiles.name: New York
state_profiles.credential_path: NYSED's matrix requires both SLP licensure/current registration and TSHH/TSSLD certification for private-agency employees and contractors providing school-age IEP speech services. A direct-school employee's educator-only exemption does not carry over automatically to this agency model.
state_profiles.school_specific_requirement: NYSED identifies fingerprinting requirements for employees of contract service providers placed in schools. Bilingual assignments add the applicable certificate extension in the credential matrix.
state_profiles.compact_relevance: See shared compact snapshot; no operational compact route established by this review.
state_profiles.practice_licensing_notes: Employment relationship changes the credential rule. The candidate record must separately verify professional registration and the applicable educator certificate; one 'license verified' flag is insufficient.
new_operator_questions: Can the initial recruiting pool supply both credentials and any bilingual extension already required by the contract?
What legal entity and contracting arrangements may deliver the chosen school service, and are separate program approvals needed?
Which district fingerprinting, clearance transfer and procurement requirements apply to the exact agency personnel model?
state_profiles.evidence_limit: The dual-credential requirement for the stated school-age agency model is explicit. Preschool, approved-program, Medicaid and independent-practice arrangements have separate nuances and are not generalized here.

entity_gate.status: SLP-specific corporate exception verified; exact operating entity and mixed-discipline model still require confirmation.
entity_gate.slp_finding: Education Law §8208(2) expressly permits corporate SLP/audiology practice when performed by licensed or exempt persons; §8208(3) requires firms offering those services to employ only licensed or exempt personnel. A blanket conclusion that an ordinary corporation is barred from the SLP-only pilot would be wrong. This does not remove the school-agency dual-credential requirement in CLS12.
entity_gate.ot_pt_finding: Do not extend the SLP exception to OT/PT. NYSED describes general corporate-practice restrictions, authorized professional entities and profession-specific exceptions. Its PT alert permits a general business corporation to act as an employment or management service, while distinguishing that activity from itself offering professional care.
entity_gate.staffing_distinction: Finding professionals for a district that employs them, providing nonclinical management, and employing therapists while contracting to deliver therapy are different models. The reviewed employment-agency examples do not expressly authorize every agency-payroll/public-school deployment. Labeling a service staffing is not proof of an exemption.
entity_gate.separate_agency_license_question: NY DOL regulates fee-based placement with third-party employers and acknowledges exceptions. Determine applicability to the chosen referral, employer-paid placement or temporary-help arrangement separately from professional-practice authority.
entity_gate.school_program_limit: The school or BOCES being an authorized provider does not establish the new contractor entity’s authority. Special-education/EI corporate waivers cover specified approved entities and services; this review does not establish eligibility for a generic school-age staffing firm.
required_decision_packet: Identify the exact legal entity, owners, professions offered, and whether the first bid is SLP only.
Map who employs the clinician, signs the school contract, invoices staffing versus therapy, controls professional decisions and owns service records.

Have New York counsel or the appropriate NYSED unit confirm the proposed contract/entity model and any applicable fee, employment-agency, entity-registration or waiver requirements before bid representations and service launch.
Review OT/PT expansion separately; do not treat the verified SLP corporate exception as multidisciplinary authority.
entity_gate.evidence_limit: This is a sourced applicability gate, not a finding that the user’s unknown entity is authorized or prohibited. No registration or legal opinion was obtained.
